prompt:
Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback


## Inline Code Comments
[0] operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller.go:62: I expect this to happen on somewhat of a regular basis. Please don't log this as ``Info`` maybe as ``Debug`` if at all.
[1] operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller_test.go:273: Useless test. We certainly do not need to test, if a struct we just created has values we assign to it. This tests go-lang more than it helps us in any way testing the controller.
[2] operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_config.go:93: Explicitly constructing a ``url.URL`` object and using ``url.UserPassword`` seems appropriate and correct
[3] operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller_test.go:324: We have ``internal/conditions`` for this kind of stuff and I am pretty sure this - again - reimplements ``meta.FindStatusCondition(conditions, conditionType)``
[4] operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_config.go:103: While functionally identical, I suggest using ``defaults`` as the second argument to this function. This makes it easier to understand what is going on when reading the code.
[5] operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_deployment.go:167: Thats what the ``k8s.io/utils/ptr`` package is for. Use that instead of reinventing functions
[6] operators/keystone/api/v1alpha1/keystone_types.go:124: I am pretty sure changing the API structs requires us to re-run ``make generate`` to re-generate the auto-generated files.
[7] internal/common/types/types.go:67: This needs to have a ``make regenerate`` as well.

Respond with ONLY the JSON object, no markdown fences, no explanation.
